5|of 318 infants (69.2%) assigned to ibuprofen and
6|202 of 318 infants (63.5%) assigned to placebo
7|(adjusted risk ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.98 to 1.20;
8|P = 0.10) (Table 2). A total of 44 of 323 infants
9|(13.6%) in the ibuprofen group and 33 of 321
10|(10.3%) in the placebo group died (adjusted risk
11|ratio, 1.32; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.90). Among the
12|infants who survived to 36 weeks of postmen-
13|strual age, moderate or severe bronchopulmo-
14|nary dysplasia was present in 176 of 274 (64.2%)
15|in the ibuprofen group and 169 of 285 (59.3%) in
16|the placebo group (adjusted risk ratio, 1.09; 95%
17|CI, 0.96 to 1.23) (Table 2 and Figs. S3 and S4).
18|Results for the primary outcome excluding in-
19|fants who received open-label medical treatment
20|without meeting the specified criteria are shown
21|in Tables S9 and S10.
22|A closed or small PDA (<1.5 mm in diame-
23|ter) at 3 weeks (18 to 24 days) of age was pres-
24|ent in 176 of 317 infants (55.5%) in the ibupro-
25|fen group and 117 of 316 (37.0%) in the placebo
26|group (adjusted risk ratio, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.30 to
27|1.74) (Table 2 and Table S11). After randomiza-
28|tion, 571 of 646 infants (88.4%) received all
29|three doses of ibuprofen or placebo (Table 3).
30|Additional secondary outcomes are shown in
31|Table 2, Figure S5, and Tables S12 and S13. A
32|total of 43 infants (13.3%) in the ibuprofen
33|group and 82 (25.5%) in the placebo group re-
34|ceived open-label medical treatment for symp-
35|toms attributable to a PDA; 9 (2.8%) and 31
36|(9.6%), respectively, received surgical treatment
37|(Table 2). The percentage of infants who re-
38|ceived any open-label treatment (for any indica-
39|tion), including surgical ligation, was 14.2% in
40|the ibuprofen group and 29.8% in the placebo
41|group; the median interval from randomization
42|to open-label treatment was 11 days (interquar-
43|tile range, 8 to 17) and 12 days (interquartile
44|range, 7 to 21), respectively. Prespecified sub-
45|group analyses of the composite primary outcome
46|and its components are shown in Figure 2A and
47|Figures S3 and S4. An additional prespecified
48|subgroup analysis of the risk of severe necrotiz-
49|ing enterocolitis (Bell's stage ≥II) according to
50|the diameter of the PDA at randomization is
51|shown in Figure 2B.
52|Safety
53|Two unforeseeable serious adverse events oc-
54|curred that were assessed as possibly related to
55|ibuprofen; one of these events was classified as
56|a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction
57|(Table S15). An additional four unforeseeable
58|serious adverse events that were assessed as not
59|related to ibuprofen occurred in the ibuprofen
60|group. Two unforeseeable serious adverse events
61|occurred in the placebo group, both of which
62|were assessed as not related to placebo. Foresee-
63|able serious adverse events were reportable dur-
64|ing the period between the first dose of ibupro-
65|fen or placebo and 7 days after the last dose
66|(Table S14).
67|Discussion
68|In this double-blind, randomized, placebo-con-
69|trolled trial involving extremely preterm infants
70|with a large PDA, we found no evidence that
71|early treatment with ibuprofen was associated with
72|a lower incidence of death or moderate or severe
